notes.name: Course Note
notes.text: Archaeology of East Asia This course explores the development of human societies in East Asia from the arrival of humans to the rise of states.  We will explore the archaeological record to discover themes such as how early hunter-gatherers used and changed local environments, the rise of horse-riding warrior tribes, the formation of cities, and the origins of elite society.  Our primary geographic focus will be North China and Mongolia, with some discussion of Siberia, Japan, and Korea.  Students will gain an appreciation for how neighbouring peoples make very different decisions about how they organize society, including the roles that culture contact, climate, and worldview play in social change or continuity.

Step 1: Request the course on ACORN. Your status will be INT. You will not be officially enrolled until you complete the remaining steps (below).
Step 2: Meet with the Supervisor and obtain their signature on a 'Supervised Study form'. Make sure the course code, supervisor name and title of the project is clearly printed on the form as this information will appear on your transcript. The Supervised Study form is available at: https://www.utsc.utoronto.ca/registrar/supervised-study-form. Your Department listed below may require additional paperwork. Students should contact the Office listed for more information.
Step 3: Submit the signed Supervised Study form by email to Arifa Nitol arifa.nitol@utoronto.ca.
Staff will update your course status on ACORN from interim (INT) to approved (APP).

notes.name: Course Note
notes.text: The International Development Studies Co-op Placement Preparation Course (COPB30) is mandatory for all new students entering the co-op program.  Students entering the program must take this course in their first year, in the Fall term.  For students entering in their second year, they must take this course in the Fall term of their second year. This course is a prerequisite for COPB31.  Students will automatically be enrolled in this course, but must ensure their timetable is clear for this registration. It is non-credit with no tuition fees attached. NOTE: Students are responsible for ensuring they understand coop course requirements, and that they do not register for other courses during the time the coop course is offered. For any issues regarding the scheduling of this course, please contact the IDS co-op office as soon as possible at 416-287-7113 or ids-coop@utsc.utoronto.ca Exclusion: COPD02H3

courses.name: Confronting Developments Racist Past and Present
Political Economy of Knowledge Technology and Development

notes.name: Course Note
notes.text: Course Description: What really happens after you press "Send" on a WhatsApp message, ask ChatGPT a question, or submit an assignment through Quercus? This course takes you inside the black boxes of the everyday digital infrastructures we depend on to explore how AI, digital platforms, and data are reshaping education, society, and international development. Through hands-on activities and shared inquiry, you'll learn to look beyond the technology itself to understand the people, infrastructures, and power relationships that shape these systems—and work together to reimagine more equitable knowledge futures.

notes.name: Course Note
notes.text: Course Description: How do the images, headlines, and platforms we encounter every day shape who counts as 'developed,' whose voices are heard, and whose are left out? IDSC08H3: Media and Development examines how traditional and new media influence development policy, how the Global South is represented, and how communities use media to tell their own stories. Drawing on current examples, from viral campaigns and streaming platforms to social media activism and the digital divide, students develop the tools to read media critically. The course is discussion-based and welcomes anyone interested in thinking carefully about media, power, and global inequality.

notes.name: Course Note
notes.text: Course Title: Worlding Development: Competing Visions along China’s Belt and Road Course Description: What is China’s Belt and Road Initiative, and why has it generated so much excitement, controversy, and anxiety? Together, we will investigate the competing stories told about China’s growing global role and ask how well they stand up to evidence. From ports, railways, and development finance to the Digital Silk Road, AI, surveillance, and data governance, the course connects a vast new topic to familiar questions about technology, power, knowledge, and development. No prior expertise on China or the BRI is expected - only curiosity and a willingness to question conventional wisdom as we explore competing development imaginaries: different ways of understanding what development is, how it should happen, by whom, and for whose benefit.

notes.name: Course Note
notes.text: Step 1: Request the course on ACORN. Your status will be INT. You will not be officially enrolled until you complete the remaining steps (below). If you are on a waitlist, you must also complete these steps in anticipation that you get enrolled into the course. Step 2: Take the placement Test and survey at: http://www.utsc.utoronto.ca/webapps/ptmandarin/ Step 3: Answer all survey questions in detail to ensure your request to enroll in a Chinese course is processed. If a question is not applicable, indicate NA. If you encounter technical difficulties at this step, click the hyperlinked 'Technical Support' at the bottom right of the webpage or contact intranet@utsc.utoronto.ca If you enroll or are admitted from the wait list after the deadline, you must fill out the questionnaire and submit it to the course instructor. Check your status through ACORN to see whether you have been approved. (APP = approval; REF = refused; INT = no decision yet) [1] You do need to take the placement/survey if you have never done so before. [2] In general, there is NO need to take the test/survey again. [3] Please do not email any instructor after you have successfully submitted your test/survey. [4] The instructors will receive an automatic email alert. [5] You will receive notification from an instructor within two business days regarding your status in the course. Your status on ACORN should be updated within 10 days of this notification. [6] Students are welcome to select these courses but will not be officially enrolled until approved. [7] Students whose level of proficiency in the language is considered unsuitable for the course will not be permitted to take the course. [8] Students are not permitted to take LGGA- and LGGB-level courses in an incorrect sequence (i.e., take a lower level course after a higher level course). Click a specific course code to read the description, including the Exclusion.

notes.name: Course Note
notes.text: SUPERVISED STUDY/RESEARCH & INDEPENDENT STUDY COURSES Step 1: Request the course on ACORN. Your status will be INT. You will not be officially enrolled until you complete the remaining steps (below). Step 2: Meet with the MGE faculty member who you hope will supervise your study/project and obtain their approval. Make sure the course code, supervisor name, and title of the project is input on the supervised study form as this information will appear on your transcript. The Supervised Study form is available at: https://www.utsc.utoronto.ca/registrar/supervised-study-form Step 3: Once complete, send the approval email from the faculty member and the completed Supervised Study form by email to the Academic Director, Economics ecoss.utsc@utoronto.ca and Jacqueline Deane jacqueline.deane@utoronto.ca Step 4: If your proposal is approved, the department will update the Registrar's Office with your Supervised Study form. Staff will update your course status on ACORN from interim (INT) to approved (APP). Your Department listed below may require additional paperwork. See policy for more details: https://www.utsc.utoronto.ca/mgmt/sites/utsc.utoronto.ca.mgmt/files/docs/Departmental%20Policy%20on%20Supervised%20Reading%20Courses%20(October%202023).pdf Economics and Management Office IC250

notes.text: Visiting students require the permission of the Academic Director. MANAGEMENT MEETING SECTION CHANGES: Students approved in a course who wish to change sections may do so on ACORN, provided there is space in the preferred section. Note: if the preferred section is full and you add yourself to the waitlist, your enrolment in the original section will be cancelled. Section changes can be made on ACORN until the last day to add courses for the session provided there is space to do so. Students are expected to enroll or waitlist for course meeting sections that fit in a conflict-free schedule. Students who knowingly enroll in a course that causes a conflict should not expect to request a section change through their Professor at a later date. Please see Calendar for overall course load limit for BBA students

notes.name: Course Note
notes.text: SUPERVISED STUDY/RESEARCH & INDEPENDENT STUDY COURSES Step 1: Request the course on ACORN. Your status will be INT. You will not be officially enrolled until you complete the remaining steps (below). Step 2: Meet with the MGE faculty member who you hope will supervise your study/project and obtain their approval. Make sure the course code, supervisor name, and title of the project is input on the supervised study form as this information will appear on your transcript. The Supervised Study form is available at: https://www.utsc.utoronto.ca/registrar/supervised-study-form . Step 3: Once complete, send the approval email from the faculty member and the completed Supervised Study form by email to the Academic Director, Economics ecoss.utsc@utoronto.ca and Jacqueline Deane jacqueline.deane@utoronto.ca Step 4: If your proposal is approved, the department will update the Registrar's Office with your Supervised Study form. Staff will update your course status on ACORN from interim (INT) to approved (APP). Your Department listed below may require additional paperwork. Economics and Management Office IC250

You will not be officially enrolled until you complete the remaining steps (below). Step 2: Meet with the Music Program Director to obtain permission to enroll in this course. You will be asked to choose a supervisor and then obtain their signature on a 'Supervised Study form'. Make sure the course code, supervisor name and title of the project is clearly printed on the form as this information will appear on your transcript. Step 3: Submit the signed Supervised Study form and additional paperwork by email to the ACM program manager, acm-pm@utsc.utoronto.ca Staff will update your course status on ACORN from interim (INT) to approved (APP). Art Culture and Media Office AA325

notes.text: SUPERVISED STUDY/RESEARCH & INDEPENDENT STUDY COURSES Step 1: Request the course on ACORN. Your status will be INT. You will not be officially enrolled until you complete the remaining steps (below). Step 2: Meet with the Supervisor and obtain their signature on a 'Supervised Study form'. Ensure the course code, supervisor's name and title of the project is clearly printed on the form as this information will appear on your transcript. The Supervised Study form is available at: https://www.utsc.utoronto.ca/registrar/supervised-study-form . Your Department listed below may require additional paperwork. Students should contact the office listed for more information. Step 3: Submit the signed Supervised Study form and additional paperwork by email to the Program Advisor sociologyadvisor.utsc@utoronto.ca. Your course status on ACORN will be updated from interim (INT) to approved (APP). Sociology Office HL206

notes.name: Course Note
notes.text: This special topics course will consider the work of contemporary artists across the globe who have addressed difficult histories, memories of trauma, loss and longing, exile and displacement. It will ask how, through their creative practices, artists have questioned history, either by revising, revisiting, or reordering it.

notes.name: Course Note
notes.text: Topic: Decolonial and Feminist Perspectives on Mental Health This course uses decolonial and feminist perspectives to critically examine how social, historical, and political contexts shape experiences of mental health, distress, and healing. We will interrogate mainstream biomedical views and learn from a range of perspectives, including Indigenous and community-based knowledges, social justice practices, and personal stories. Topics include gendered experiences of mental health, trauma-informed care, institutionalization and psychiatric systems, community-based mental health, non-Western healing traditions, and decolonial psychosocial approaches to resistance and healing. The course aims to deepen students' understanding of the multiple ways in which power and intersecting systems of oppression affect mental health as well as explore more just and equitable approaches to care and wellbeing.
